clue.text: One does nothing to make such treatment effective

definitions.text: One does nothing to make such treatment effective

parts.words: One does nothing to make such treatment effective
parts.note: the patient's idleness is itself the medicine: a therapy whose whole point is that you lie about and do nothing

explanation.surface: A wry remark about a therapy that only works if the patient stays idle.
explanation.definitionFit: A cure by rest is a medical regime of enforced inactivity, so doing nothing is exactly what makes it work.

clue.text: A long way off getting a rising service

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: the RAF, Britain's Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: Someone far from home, perhaps waiting for a church service or a promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rising' reads the service upwards. The RAF is Britain's Royal Air Force.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar is an adverb meaning at or to a great distance, a synonym of a long way off.

clue.text: Slightly exaggerate an account and blush

definitions.meaning: to embellish or slant a story is to give it a tint beyond the plain facts
to go red in the face, as the cheeks take on a tint

explanation.surface: A storyteller who embroiders the truth and goes red when found out.
explanation.definitionFit: To colour a report is to distort it a little, and to colour up is to flush red with embarrassment.

clue.text: Experience initial difficulty in speech-making

parts.note: reads like stage fright before an oration, but initial means the first sounds of words are repeated as one talks

explanation.surface: A nervous speaker struggles at the start of a public address.
explanation.definitionFit: A speech impediment in which the opening sounds of words are repeated is exactly difficulty with initials when speaking.

clue.text: The deep — place for many catches

definitions.meaning: in cricket, the deep is the area far from the batsman near the boundary
the far part of a cricket or baseball field where fielders take many catches

explanation.surface: Seems to be about the ocean, where fishermen land big catches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The deep' and 'catches' suggest the sea and fishing; both are cricket terms here.
explanation.definitionFit: The outer area of a cricket ground is called the deep, and fielders there take many catches.

clue.text: Jovial acknowledgement of a bad standard

parts.note: jovial means jolly, cheerful
roger is radio-speak for message received and understood

explanation.surface: A cheerful nod of agreement given to some poor level of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standard' looks like a level of quality, but it is a flag: the skull-and-crossbones flown by pirates, who are bad people.
explanation.definitionFit: The pirates' skull-and-crossbones flag is a standard, a banner, flown by villains.

clue.text: Game needing a light touch with the whip

parts.note: a tip is a light tap or touch
the cat-o'-nine-tails, a whip, is called the cat

explanation.surface: A sport, perhaps riding, that requires a deft hand with the whip.
explanation.walkthrough: Tipcat is an old children's game in which a tapered piece of wood is tipped into the air with a stick and then struck.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipcat is a traditional street game played with a short tapered stick and a bat.

clue.text: It's safer not to stray by the shore

indicators.note: to stray is to wander from the right path, so the letters wander out of order

parts.note: the fodder as written

explanation.surface: Safety advice: don't wander off when you are down at the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: A seafront is the stretch of a coastal town facing the sea, along the shore.

clue.text: More work repairing high-class patio

parts.note: U is the old abbreviation for upper class, socially acceptable

indicators.note: repairing means putting something back together, here the letters in a new order

parts.note: the fodder as written

explanation.surface: A posh paved terrace needs more work to fix it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More' is not 'extra' but Sir Thomas More, whose famous work is the book of that title. 'repairing' rearranges U plus PATIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Thomas More's best-known book, published in 1516, describes an ideal island society.

clue.text: The highlight of the Nativity

parts.note: highlight is taken literally: the bright light shining high over Bethlehem in the Christmas story

explanation.surface: The best moment of a school Christmas play.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Nativity story a brilliant light in the sky guided the wise men, literally the high light of the scene.

clue.text: Unfit, so ousted

definitions.meaning: removed from one's position, literally evicted from where one was

explanation.surface: Someone sacked because they were not up to the job.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means inappropriate, and read literally it means turned out of one's position.

clue.text: Boatswain's mate found at the end of the line

definitions.meaning: naval slang for the chief boatswain's mate on a Royal Navy ship

definitions.text: found at the end of the line
definitions.meaning: the sprung stop at the end of a railway track

explanation.surface: A ship's officer turns up at the railway terminus.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'line' is a railway line: the sprung stops at the end of the track have this name.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Royal Navy the chief bosun's mate is so called, and railway track ends in a shock-absorbing stop of the same name.

clue.text: Annual pop festival

parts.note: pop is not music but dad, so this is the yearly occasion honouring him

explanation.surface: Sounds like a yearly music event such as Glastonbury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pop festival' suggests rock music; 'pop' is a word for father.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearly day in June when children honour their fathers, or pops, is an annual festival for dad.

clue.text: Former partner to create trouble, leading to censure

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

indicators.note: to trouble is to disturb, so the letters of the next word are stirred up

parts.note: the fodder as written

explanation.surface: A former spouse stirs up trouble, which leads to public criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' is the anagram signal working on 'create', though in the surface it looks like a noun the ex causes.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to denounce or curse someone, a strong form of condemnation.

clue.text: The environment is declining

definitions.meaning: surroundings, the backdrop or location of something
going down, as the sun does in the evening

explanation.surface: A gloomy claim that the natural world is going downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'environment' suggests ecology; it means surroundings, as for a play or a jewel.
explanation.definitionFit: A setting is the surroundings of something, and a sun that is going down is said to be in the act of sinking.

clue.text: Mark closely and upset the club three-quarters

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a baton is a short club or truncheon
E, N and E are three compass points, or quarters: east-north-east

explanation.surface: Instructions to watch carefully, then knock over three-quarters of a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns BATON into NOTAB; the three quarters are compass points, ENE.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin phrase, abbreviated NB, tells the reader to take careful note of something.

clue.text: Slowly executed movements get a soldier into difficulties

indicators.note: into means the following pieces go inside the word for difficulties

parts.note: ados are fusses or troubles
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier in trouble is made to do drill moves at a slow pace.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagios are pieces or movements of music, or dance passages, performed at a slow tempo.

clue.text: Public company that could be mine

parts.note: open means public, available to all
the cast is the company of actors in a play

explanation.surface: A public company offers a stake that one could own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks like a possessive; it is a pit. The definition describes the answer, which is a kind of mine, worked from the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Opencast describes a mine dug from the surface rather than underground, so such a pit could be mine of this type.

clue.text: I call round on pressing business

indicators.note: round means the word for call surrounds the next piece

parts.note: to ring is to telephone, to call
taken as written

explanation.surface: A busy person phones round about some urgent matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pressing' looks like urgent, but it means pressing clothes with a hot iron.
explanation.definitionFit: Smoothing clothes with a hot iron is literally a business of pressing.

clue.text: One who's left without credit

parts.note: sounds like someone denied a bank loan, but means a soldier who has run away in disgrace

explanation.surface: Someone stranded with no money or loan.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier who abandons his post leaves without honour, with no credit to his name.

clue.text: Fears losing head and making blunders

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter is dropped from the word for fears

parts.note: terrors are great fears

explanation.surface: Someone panicking and making mistakes as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' drops the T from TERRORS.
explanation.definitionFit: Errors are mistakes, which is what blunders are.

clue.text: Animal hunt

definitions.meaning: a small weasel-like creature kept for catching rabbits
to search persistently, to rummage about

explanation.surface: A two-word note about wildlife and the chase.
explanation.definitionFit: The ferret is a domesticated polecat, and to ferret about is to search for something.

clue.text: Calif's worried about revenue

indicators.note: worried means agitated, so the letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: the fodder read as Calif is, so the S counts

explanation.surface: A caliph, a Muslim ruler, frets about state income.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges CALIFS. A calif (caliph) is a Muslim ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiscal means relating to public revenue and taxation.

clue.text: Finance companies issuing notes, not silver

definitions.text: Finance companies issuing notes, not silver

parts.words: Finance companies issuing notes, not silver
parts.note: brass is slang for money and bands are companies playing musical notes; not silver contrasts them with silver bands

explanation.surface: Banks printing paper money instead of minting coins.
explanation.walkthrough: Brass is British slang for cash; the 'notes' are musical ones, and silver bands are a rival kind of ensemble with silver-plated instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: Groups of trumpeters and tuba players are companies producing musical notes on brass rather than silver instruments.

clue.text: Wine, or pop

definitions.meaning: a white wine from the German Rhineland
to pawn, as in popping something at the pawnbroker's

explanation.surface: A choice of drinks: something alcoholic or fizzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pop' looks like a soft drink; it is British slang for pawning.
explanation.definitionFit: Hock is a German white wine, and to hock or pop goods is to pawn them.

clue.text: Depression characteristic of the camel

definitions.meaning: a fit of sulking or gloom, as in having or getting the sulks
the fatty lump on a camel's back

explanation.surface: A low mood that seems to go with being a camel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' looks like a hollow, the opposite of a lump; it is British slang for a sulk, 'the hump'.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a fit of gloom is called the hump, and a camel is known for the lump on its back.

clue.text: Roadworks in order

indicators.note: the second half of Roadworks, read as a verb: road works, so those four letters are reworked

parts.note: the fodder as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Roadworks are in good order.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word 'Roadworks' splits: 'works' rearranges ROAD into ORDA, and IN follows unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: To ordain is to decree or command something officially.

clue.text: Almost a hit with the girl next door?

parts.note: near means close by, as a neighbour is
a miss is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A suitor almost succeeds with the girl next door.
explanation.definitionFit: A near miss is an attempt that just fails to hit its target.
